description: Tunnel certificates of the Relay Specification v0 (draft), RELAY-v0.md section 5.4, as the chain of a certificate response. Each case: chain (DER, base64url without padding, the issued certificate first), not_after of the response, the tunnel key of the request, trust_domain and home_id of the installation, requested_at (when the request was sent), received_at (when the response arrived), earlier_not_before (the latest notBefore of the tunnel certificates issued to the installation before, or null), and whether the certificate is valid. Valid: one to four certificates; the issued one has the tunnel key; its subject alternative name extension is critical and is byte for byte one URI, spiffe://<trust_domain>/home/<home_id>/gateway; its subject is empty; notAfter equals not_after, is after notBefore and received_at and at most 24 hours after notBefore; notBefore is no earlier than 5 minutes before requested_at, no later than received_at and later than earlier_not_before (issuance lies between the two times, so a notBefore outside these bounds breaks the rule of 5 minutes before issuance or of no later than issuance); cA=false (also without a basic constraints extension); key usage digitalSignature alone and critical; extended key usage serverAuth and clientAuth and no other. Where the chain holds a second certificate, it issued the first and carries a name constraint whose permitted URI subtree is trust_domain alone. Valid means that the certificate meets section 5.4 as the live test checks it; a gateway has to refuse only what fails the checks section 5.4 lists for it. Whether the serial number has 64 random bits cannot be seen in one certificate. The keys are test keys; their private parts are in relay/conformance/keys/test-keys.private.json. Generated with go run ./tools/vectors relay-certificate.
